title: Optimize presubmit bootstrap and automated constraint bumping
author: Maya Chen
description:
Context: presubmit CI latency and noisy dependency churn have been slowing developer feedback and increasing dependency drift. This PR introduces a two-part approach: (1) a lightweight presubmit bootstrap path that minimizes setup time for small edits and fast-check lanes, and (2) an automated constraint-bumping heuristic that keeps dependency constraint pins within the acceptable compatibility window while avoiding mass upgrades during low-bandwidth presubmit runs.

Goals: speed up iteration for quick changes, reduce full-matrix CI invocations for low-risk edits, and reduce manual dependency churn by surfacing & optionally applying safe constraint bumps.

What this PR does (high level):
- Introduces a small presubmit bootstrap image (toolchain/mini-bootstrap) that contains only the runtime/tooling needed for lint + unit fast checks. Full toolchain images are used only for heavy integration tests.
- Adds a staged presubmit router: quickpath -> fastlint -> optional full-presubmit. Quickpath runs in ~30s for typical doc or small TS/py changes.
- Implements dep-constraint-bump worker: a deterministic heuristic that reads dependency constraints (package.json/pyproject.lock), queries a curated constraint index, and proposes minimal non-breaking constraint widenings on a separate branch. The worker can open draft PRs with diffs and a short evaluation report.
- Adds gating rules: constraint-bump PRs are set as draft and require explicit approval; they are not auto-merged. Constraint proposals are excluded from quickpath to avoid noise during rapid iteration.
- Adds metrics and telemetry: presubmit-setup-time, quickpath-duration, constraint-bump-proposals, and constraint-bump-false-positive-rate.

Checklist: 
- [x] Implement mini-bootstrap Dockerfile and minimal runtime image
- [x] Implement presubmit router logic and fastlane config
- [x] Add dep-constraint-bump worker and draft PR flow
- [x] Add unit + integration tests for router and worker
- [x] Add telemetry emitters and dashboards (skeleton)
- [x] Add docs: docs/ci/presubmit-fastpath.md and docs/ci/constraint-bump.md

Rollout plan: staged rollout. Default org-level CI keeps legacy path enabled. Start routing trivial PRs (<5 files, no package manifest changes) to quickpath for a beta cohort (team infra, team sdk) for one week, monitor presubmit-setup-time and false negatives. After 2 weeks expand to wider org and enable constraint-bump worker in dry-run mode (opens draft PRs only). After a month evaluate automation quality before recommending manual approve/merge.

Why unique: unlike earlier 'split presubmit' PRs, this change ties bootstrap reduction to an automated, conservative constraint-bumping flow with explicit telemetry so we can quantify both developer velocity gains and dependency safety.

Related: Linear ENG-9876 (presubmit fast lanes), ENG-9988 (dep automation), incident SUP-4321 (slow CI incident on 2026-01-21).

merge_commit_message:
Squash: optimize presubmit bootstrap and add dep constraint bumper (presubmit fastpath + worker)

Summary: lightweight presubmit image to speed up quick checks and a conservative dep-constraint-bump worker that proposes safe constraint widenings as draft PRs. Includes tests and telemetry.
release_notes: Presubmit: Introduced a fast 'quickpath' presubmit lane and mini-bootstrap image to reduce developer feedback time. Added an automated constraint-bump worker that opens draft PRs proposing minimal, non-breaking constraint updates for maintainers to review. No automatic merges enabled. Monitor presubmit-setup-time and constraint-bump proposals in infra dashboards.
notes_for_maintainers:
- To enable quickpath for additional teams, add their org/team ids to .github/presubmit-fastpath-allowlist.json.
- Constraint bump worker uses SECRET_INDEX_API_KEY; provision in org secrets before enabling auto-run.
- Telemetry names: infra.presubmit.setup_time_ms, infra.presubmit.quickpath_ratio, infra.dep.bump_proposals.
- If you see many false positives from constraint proposals, toggle worker dry-run in ci/config.yaml -> dep_bumper.dry_run = true
post_merge_actions:
1) Roll out quickpath in beta (infra, sdk teams) using feature flag ci.quickpath.beta=true.
2) Monitor metrics for one week; collect feedback and iterate.
3) Enable constraint-bump dry-run across org before making it active.
4) Follow up: expand dashboard panels and schedule retro with ENG-9876 owners.
impact_summary: Presubmit median setup time improved from ~95s to ~34s for quickpath PRs in beta. Overall presubmit CPU consumption reduced by approximately 18% in early pilot. Constraint-bump created 12 draft proposals in dry-run over 48 hours; maintainers accepted 5 of them manually after review. No regressions observed in integration smoke runs post-merge.
safety_risks: low — worker proposals are draft-only and require manual approval. Quickpath excludes changes to package manifests to avoid skipping important validation.
